verifications.claim: NASA's Artemis II mission is launching no earlier than April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT' on April 1, 2026 after delays from early February; R2: 'April 1 between 6:24 p.m. ET and 8:24 p.m. ET'; R4: Launch at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm launch occurred on April 1, 2026, after prior delays, directly supporting no earlier date.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since Apollo'; R3: 'NASA’s first mission with crew aboard the SLS rocket and Orion'; R4: 'first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign'
verifications.reasoning: All sources explicitly state Artemis II as first crewed Artemis mission following uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II sends four astronauts on a ~10-day journey around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about nine and a half days'; R2: 'more than 600,000-mile, 10-day journey around the moon'; R4: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe four astronauts on ~10-day lunar flyby mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the SLS rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket making its first crewed launch'; R3: 'first mission with crew aboard the SLS rocket'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first crewed SLS launch, testing it with crew.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion capsule, which is making only its second flight — and its first with a crew on board'; R2: 'test critical spacecraft systems'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm first crewed Orion flight, testing systems.

verifications.claim: The crew of Artemis II consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; identical in all sources
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew listed consistently across all references.

verifications.claim: An objective of Artemis II is to test life-support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'check out all of (Orion's) environmental control, life support systems'; R2: 'test life support, communications, and navigation systems'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated as test objective in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: An objective of Artemis II is to verify deep-space navigation.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'communications, navigation, propulsion and life support systems'; R2: 'test life support, communications, and navigation systems'
verifications.reasoning: Navigation systems testing explicitly mentioned in deep-space context.

verifications.claim: An objective of Artemis II is to perform lunar observations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'getting an unprecedented view of the far side of the moon'; R2: 'observing and photographing the far side of the moon'; R8: 'lunar observations'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm lunar observations during flyby.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R2: 'first time humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 (1972).

verifications.claim: Artemis II aims to travel farther than any human before.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'travel farther from Earth than anyone before them'; R2: 'set a record for the farthest distance humans have ever traveled from Earth: 252,000 miles'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state it will exceed previous human distance records (e.g., Apollo 13).

verifications.claim: The launch site for Artemis II is Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'launching from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, using the historic Launch Complex 39B'; consistent across sources
verifications.reasoning: All sources specify Kennedy Space Center, Pad 39B.

verifications.claim: The Artemis III landing mission is scheduled for 2028
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis III... will now be a crewed rendezvous mission... Artemis IV through V, are now planned for 2028 and will land astronauts'; R8: 'Artemis IV intends to mark the first crewed Moon landing... by 2028'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state Artemis III changed to rendezvous (no landing), with landings starting Artemis IV in 2028.
